Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the AetherCloud Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register by pressing star then one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing AetherCloud's results for the Q3 FY2024. With me on the call are Jordan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Linden, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Mia Chen, Chief Product Officer; and Raj Patel, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Hale.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. AetherCloud delivered another strong Q3, marked by significant growth in our core cloud business and increasing adoption of our innovative AI solutions.

During the quarter, our priorities were focused on six key areas:
1. Expanding our global cloud infrastructure footprint.
2. Driving innovation in serverless computing.
3. Enhancing our cybersecurity offerings.
4. Strengthening our partnerships with leading ISVs.
5. Improving customer satisfaction and retention.
6. Investing in our talent pool and fostering a culture of innovation.

We made substantial strides in broadening our global presence, adding new availability zones in high-growth regions like APAC and EMEA to support sovereign cloud needs and reduce latency for AI workloads. This expansion has positioned us to capture more enterprise demand, particularly in regulated sectors.

Now I'll turn the call over to Sarah Linden to provide a detailed review of our financial performance.

Sarah Linden:
Thank you, Jordan. We are pleased with our financial results for the Q3. Revenue increased by 28% year-over-year to $25.2 billion, driven by strong demand for our cloud services. Our gross margin was 72.5%, reflecting our focus on operational efficiency. Our operating margin was 31%.

Let me elaborate on our overall gross margin trends and the key drivers behind them. Our GAAP gross margin expanded significantly year-over-year, reaching levels that highlight the strength of our hyperscale infrastructure, tight operational control, and deliberate move toward higher-margin AI and enterprise services. Excluding stock-based compensation and amortization, our non-GAAP gross margin hit 33.1% for the quarter, with full-year progress showing steady improvement to 31.2% from 29.8% last year—our third straight year of gains, even as we ramped up capacity for booming AI needs.

Scale efficiencies from our over 120 availability zones in 35 regions have pushed utilization in mature data centers above 85%, up from 78% a few years back. As AI training and inference workloads explode on platforms like AetherAI, fixed costs like depreciation and power spread across much larger revenue volumes. There was some sequential softening due to upfront investments in NVIDIA H100 GPU setups and elevated energy prices from supply constraints.

Shifting product mix provided the biggest lift, with about 140 basis points of full-year expansion. IaaS revenues from AetherCompute grew 22% but dropped to 42% of total revenue as customers shifted to PaaS and SaaS options yielding over 45% margins. AetherML, with managed Kubernetes and serverless endpoints, made up over 30% of Q4 revenue and grew 28%, much like peers' AI services that carry 10-15 point premiums over basic storage at around 25%. Enterprise analytics via AetherDataLake, rivaling Snowflake, hit 55% margins thanks to software efficiencies. Our AI-First strategy bundles GPUs with orchestration to cut customer TCO by 30% while holding pricing firm, and we see AI/ML reaching 40% of revenue by FY2025 for another 100-150 basis points in margins.

Cost controls added 80 basis points, led by Gen3 AetherGraviton Arm chips powering 35% of instances with 40% better price-performance and 25% less power per FLOP, hitting 92% utilization on LLM clusters. Liquid cooling in 60% of new facilities slashed cooling expenses by 37% for dense AI racks. We've locked in 70% renewable energy through deals with Ørsted and NextEra, aiming for carbon-neutral by 2028, while depreciation per revenue dollar fell 12%. Utilization analytics prevent overbuilds.

Regionally, North America at 55% of revenue led with 35.2% margins from dense hyperscale and sovereign clouds. EMEA hit 33.8%, up 180 basis points on GDPR AI services. APAC at 25% revenue trailed at 28.5% from competitive pricing against Alibaba, but edge nodes will boost emerging margins by 200 basis points by FY2025. FX and bandwidth hikes offset some gains, but 118% net retention shows pricing strength amid 20-25% discounts on AI commitments.

For FY2024, we expect non-GAAP gross margins of 32.5-33.5%, or 130-230 basis points up, with 25% revenue growth and $22 billion capex at 18% of revenue.

Next, I'd like to introduce Dr. Elena Vasquez, who will provide an update on our technology initiatives.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sarah. On the technology front, we made significant progress in several areas. We successfully launched our next-generation AetherCloud platform, which offers enhanced performance and scalability.

A key highlight is our compute and storage capacity utilization rates, which hit record levels and demonstrate our prowess in matching massive infrastructure to surging AI and enterprise demand. Global compute utilization reached 82.4%, up 450 basis points year-over-year and 210 sequentially—our best in three years across x86, Arm Graviton4, and GPU fleets for H100 and A100.

By workload, general-purpose instances averaged 79%, AI/ML accelerators at 28% of capacity blazed at 91% with partners like Anthropic, and HPC held at 85% for pharma simulations. Storage utilization climbed to 91.2%, led by 93% in object storage for data lakes and 88% in block for databases.

Regionally, US East led at 84% compute and 92% storage, EU at 80% and 90%, APAC jumped to 79% compute amid expansions, and emerging areas ramped from 65-70%. AI forecasting at 95% accuracy enables spot utilization at 35%, PUEs under 1.15 with liquid cooling, and storage tiering boost density 40%. Customer right-sizing freed 12% capacity for AI.

This supports $65 billion FY2024 capex, targeting 80-85% utilization ahead of peers, fueled by $200 billion GenAI industry spend.

Now, I'll pass it over to Mia Chen for a product roadmap update.

Mia Chen:
Thank you, Elena. We are excited about the market reception to our new AetherML offering. This product is designed to address the evolving needs of our customers in the enterprise AI sector.

I'll now hand it over to Raj Patel to discuss our marketing initiatives.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Mia. We have been focused on driving brand awareness and generating demand for our solutions. Our recent marketing campaigns have been highly effective in reaching our target audience, particularly through targeted promotions that accelerated customer growth.

Speaking of which, our pricing strategies and discounting programs have been pivotal in fueling this momentum. In this competitive hyperscale landscape, we've honed a multi-tiered approach—PAYG at $0.024 per vCPU-hour, 40-60% off RIs and Savings Plans with 22% uptake surge, and 70-90% spot discounts yielding 82% utilization. Consumption pricing now at 65% of revenue aligns with GenAI, undercutting rivals on inference at $0.0012 per 1,000 tokens.

Discounts averaged 18% for new logos and 25% for expansions, driving 42% customer adds to 18,500, 15% ARPU lift to $167K, and 128% NRR despite 180 basis point margin dip to 72.5%—offset by 95% utilization and 22% CAC drop. Low-discount cohorts retain at 98%, with 65% expanding to containers.

North America stays conservative at 8-12%, EMEA aggressive at 22% for share gains, APAC at 25-35% with free egress promos. AI dynamic pricing via SageAI boosts win rates 14%, predictive plans add savings, and bundles capture GenAI spend. We'll sustain 15-20% discounts for 25% share, launching savings marketplaces.

Back to Jordan.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, Raj. We are confident that our strong financial performance, innovative technology, and talented team will enable us to continue to deliver exceptional value to our customers and shareholders.

Before wrapping up, let me touch on our energy efficiency and sustainability initiatives, which are core to our long-term strategy. With data center capacity growing 15% CAGR, energy is 40% of emissions but a key for costs and differentiation—saving $185 million in Q3 alone, cutting power OpEx to 14.2%.

Our PUE hit 1.13, beating 1.55 benchmarks via 45% liquid immersion for AI, Graviton4 cutting IT load 18 TWh, and WUE at 0.12 L/kWh with recycling. Renewables at 92%, with 4.2 GW PPAs including offshore wind and solar-storage; EMEA at 98%, APAC improving. SMRs for 1 GW baseload, NimbusOptix for carbon-aware scheduling dropping intensity to 24 gCO2e/kWh.

ESG customers at 28% of top accounts shift 15-20% more to Sustainable Compute, adding $320 million bookings at 142% NRR and compressing COGS to $0.23/hour. $2.8 billion capex for cooling, renewables, capture, photonics targets PUE 1.08 and $750 million savings.

With that, let's open the call for questions. Sarah, one more thing on guidance before Q&A.

Sarah Linden:
Absolutely, Jordan. For the cloud segment at 82% of revenue, Q4 guidance is $2.85 billion to $2.90 billion, 29% YoY growth; full-year $10.85 billion to $10.95 billion, 27% up. Driven by 35% compute growth from H100/Blackwell, 32% storage, 24% PaaS; Americas 28%, EMEA 35%, APAC 30%; NRR to 120%, margins 72-73%.

Full company Q4 $3.45 billion to $3.50 billion, 25% growth; FY2024 $13.25 billion to $13.35 billion, 24% up. $1.2 billion capex supports this.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Ben Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Ben Carter:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On gross margins, with the mix shift to AI and utilization gains, how should we think about the sustainability of that 32.5-33.5% FY2024 guide amid capex ramp and energy costs?

Jordan Hale:
Thanks, Ben. Sarah covered the drivers well—AI mix to 40% by FY2025, Graviton efficiencies, liquid cooling, and 85%+ utilization give us durable tailwinds. Regional investments in APAC will accrete over time, and renewables hedge energy inflation. We're outpacing peers through disciplined execution, positioning for 100-150 bps further upside.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong:
Great, thanks. On guidance, the cloud segment raise is impressive—can you unpack the AI contribution and any risks from GPU supply or non-AI softening?

Sarah Linden:
Thanks, Lisa. AI is the accelerant, with inference over 40% of Q4 compute via Aether TensorFlow/PyTorch, RPO at $28 billion. Storage and PaaS add momentum. Risks like FX or competition are baked in, but $5.2 billion cash and FCF strength let us flex. We're guiding conservatively against 21% market growth.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you for your insightful questions. We are committed to transparency and open communication with our investors.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
